reason: The wet methane needs to be stored dry and cold, so the methane liquefier seems like the natural place to start.
expectation: I expect the plant to remove moisture and cool the methane for storage, though I don't know whether this will complete the goal in one step.

alternatives.reason: The oxygen also needs its own cold store, but I chose to follow the methane stream first.

effect: The methane is now dry and stored as a liquid, though producing the rest will take months. The oxygen store remains to be made.
reaction: The moisture removal before liquefaction made the storage process clearer.
reason: The oxygen liquefier is the only available combination and matches the remaining goal.
expectation: I expect it to cool the oxygen into a separate liquid store, though I don't know whether that completes the goal immediately.

effect: The oxygen is now stored separately, completing both goals and establishing the beginning of the propellant supply for ascent.
reaction: The two separate stores made the distinction between fuel and oxidizer clear, though the final action was predictable.

mostWorthwhile.text: Liquefying the methane was most worthwhile because the explanation connected drying it first with storing it cold and clarified that production will take months.

leastWorthwhile.text: Liquefying the oxygen felt least engaging because it was the only remaining combination and closely followed the methane step.

surprise.text: I had not expected the methane stream to need its residual water removed before liquefaction.

arbitrary.text: Neither action felt arbitrary; each matched a stated storage goal.

continue.text: I would continue to see how the distant core is collected and the specimens make it home, though this chapter's choices were straightforward.
